text:
Source Document: Python 3.12 Documentation - Built-in Types and Asynchronous I/O > Section: Python 3.12: Concurrency and Asyncio Framework

Python 3.12 introduces major performance improvements to asyncio event loops, sub-interpreters, and low-overhead monitoring. Asyncio provides the foundation for writing single-threaded concurrent code using coroutines, multiplexing I/O access over sockets and other resources.

text:
Source Document: Python 3.12 Documentation - Built-in Types and Asynchronous I/O > Section: Task Management and TaskGroup

The asyncio.TaskGroup context manager provides a reliable way to run a group of concurrent tasks. If any task fails with an exception, remaining tasks in the group are automatically canceled, preventing leaked background coroutines.

text:
Source Document: Python 3.12 Documentation - Built-in Types and Asynchronous I/O > Section: Coroutines and Event Loops

Coroutines declared with async def syntax are executed by scheduling them on an event loop or awaiting them inside another coroutine. The event loop is the core of every asyncio application.
